title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-debug-scratchpad-5
content:
Objective: record commands, logs, hypotheses and quick experiments for the Dedicated GPU pool autoscale/warmup thrash seen during the 2024-11-06 morning burst. Quick notes for triage and next steps.

Symptom summary:
- Customer-facing latency spikes (100–400ms P50 -> P95 token latency increased), followed by request queueing and 503s from the route fallback.
- Autoscaler spun up N new nodes but pods stayed in Pending for ~90–180s before scheduling -> cold-starts & warmup mismatch.
- Observed CPU at 70% on control-plane nodes, and node-creation churn (lots of provisioning/termination events) -> capacity thrash.
- Warmup jobs (sidecar priming) not running early enough, leading to model load latency on first requests.

Timeline & quick events (UTC):
- 2024-11-06 08:03: first latency alert from synthetic canary (p50 up).
- 2024-11-06 08:05 autoscaler started scale-up for pool "dedicated-gpu-eu-west-2" (requested +6 GPUs).
- 2024-11-06 08:06 lots of Pending pods (k8s state) and kube-scheduler backoffs.
- 2024-11-06 08:08 node provisioning events from cloud provider (spin-up) reported.
- 2024-11-06 08:10 first new node Ready; but model-serving pods scheduled at 08:11 and then crashloop (OOM or model load errors).
- 2024-11-06 08:14 fallback routes engaged for some customers.
- 2024-11-06 08:25 scale-down started prematurely, then again scale-up at 08:27 -> oscillation.

Commands & outputs I ran (copy-paste raw):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -o wide --selector=pool=dedicated-gpu-eu-west-2
  -> many pods in Pending, some CrashLoopBackOff. Pod events show "0/8 nodes are available: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" initially then later "node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeAffinity" for a subset.

- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-45-12
  -> Taints: gpu-ready=false:NoSchedule (we add taint and then allow taint-tolerations on serving DaemonSet). Observed newer nodes missing the taint because bootstrap script didn't finish.

- gcloud compute instances describe gpu-eu-west-2-06 --format=json
  -> status: RUNNING. startupScript logs (serial-port-1) show cloud-init finished, but kubelet join logs show "failed to register node: timed out contacting apiserver" for ~40s.

- kubectl logs <model-pod> -n redwood-serving
  -> error snippets: "failed to mmap weights: invalid argument" and "cuda driver mismatch: kernel module not loaded" on two different pods (different node builds).

Observations / likely root causes (brain dump):
- Node bootstrap drift: some nodes come up without correct GPU drivers or kubelet config (we saw CUDA driver issues and missing taint). Makes pods crash or unschedulable -> autoscaler keeps adding more nodes to meet pending pods, creating thrash.
- Warmup ordering: autoscaler adds nodes, pods schedule but model container starts and attempts to load weights without warmed cache (no prefix/KV priming) -> long model load time and readiness probes fail, causing restart/backoff.
- Scale-down policy too aggressive: cooldowns set too short, so scale-down triggers during transient low load; combined with slow warmup causes repeated up/down.
- Scheduler affinity/anti-affinity bug: some pods have nodeAffinity requiring 'gpu-generation: v2' label; new nodes sometimes lack label because bootstrap is delayed. That causes some pods to remain Pending while autoscaler continues to add nodes.
- Control-plane CPU pressure: kube-scheduler and controller-manager CPU saturation delays scheduling decisions -> further prolong Pending state.

Quick experiments tried and notes: (what worked / didn't)
1) Manual cordon/uncordon new nodes to force re-run of bootstrap: no consistent effect.
2) Rebooting one bad node -> after reboot, node registered with correct taints and driver loaded. Suggests bootstrap race on driver install.
3) Bumped node bootstrap VM image to include pre-baked NVIDIA driver and containerd config on a single test node -> model pods started faster and readiness succeeded. Promising but needs validation across images.
4) Increased HPA cooldown (scaleDownStabilizationSeconds) from 60s -> 300s in experiment cluster -> oscillation reduced but still observed when many Pending pods accumulate.

Important log excerpts (redacted):
- "Nov 06 08:09:42 kubelet[1122]: E1126 08:09:42.123 kubelet.go:123] failed to start plugin: driver not found"
- "Nov 06 08:11:01 model-server[1]: Error: failed to mmap weights: invalid argument; path=/models/llama-7b/weights.bin"
- "Nov 06 08:12:15 kube-scheduler[348]: Warning: scheduling latency high: avg 1500ms; backoff retry for pod default/model-abc"

Hypotheses to validate (ranked):
1) Bootstrap race causes nodes to miss driver install/label/taint -> primary cause of Pending/crashloop. Validate by instrumenting bootstrap logs and adding a staged readiness check that posts to /health when all bootstrap steps completed.
2) Autoscaler config lacks awareness of node bootstrap time -> it measures only Requested v.s. Ready capacity. Need to configure scale-up delay and cool-down to account for long node init (or change to use CA with unready Node handling).
3) Model warmup is synchronous at container start causing long readiness times; we should move heavy warmup to an async sidecar or perform proactive warmup on new nodes (pre-warm pools).
4) Scheduler is CPU-throttled; increase request/limit for kube-scheduler/controller-manager or move to dedicated control-plane nodes.

Follow-ups / action items (owner -> Asha / collaborators):
- [Asha] Add more verbose bootstrap logs to GCE startup script and push to stackdriver with node metadata. (PR: infra/images#412)
- [Marco] Build an image variant with preinstalled NVIDIA driver + container runtime config and test at scale. (linked PR: github.com/redwood/infra-images/pull/419)
- [Renee] Tweak autoscaler policy in staging: scaleDownStabilizationSeconds=600, maxSurge=2, and enable balance-sim. Run load test 2hr morning window.
- [Infra] Add a pre-warm job that creates a small pool of EC2/GCE GPU nodes during predicted traffic spikes (experiment feature flag).
- [SRE] Increase kube-scheduler request CPU from 100m -> 300m in cluster-alpha and observe scheduling latency.

Things to capture next time (checklist for post-incident):
- Collect full startup logs (serial port) for any node that failed to register.
- Correlate cloud provider provisioning timestamps with k8s node ReadyTime and pod scheduled time.
- Capture model container stdout/stderr for first 5 restarts.
- Enable driver install success metric and kubelet join timing histogram.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Might be worth switching to node auto-provisioning with baked AMI that includes drivers, remove heavy runtime ops on boot.
- Consider switching scale decision to base on Ready pods rather than Pending pods count to avoid reacting to bootstrap delays. But need to ensure we still scale sufficiently proactively.
- Check if the warmup sidecar code (warmup-service) can be given a higher priorityClass so it runs earlier on node.

Unresolved questions:
- Why are some nodes missing taint on bootstrap? (race in our bootstrap script or cloud-init ordering).
- Is model weight file mmap failure due to kernel param or filesystem mount (ephemeral fs upsizing)?

Good references:
- confluence:runbooks/dedicated-gpu-autoscale (runbook draft)
- JIRA-ENG-3124 (incident ticket)
- infra/images PR list: github.com/redwood/infra-images/pulls

Next sync: quick huddle 2024-11-09 09:30 UTC in #infra-gpu. Will bring initial bootstrap logs and experiment results.

End of scratchpad.
